entries.principle_source: OECD Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence, OECD/LEGAL/0449 (adopted 2019, amended 2024), principle 1.4 (a); a recommendation, not binding law
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan 'On artificial intelligence' No. 230-VIII of 17 November 2025
entries.provision: Art. 15 p. 2 sub. 2 (owners must ensure safety and reliability of the AI system, incl. protection against failures); also Law 'On personal data and their protection' No. 94-V of 21 May 2013, Art. 12 p. 1 (only data necessary and sufficient for the task)
entries.why_here: Part 1 used only clean profiles (0 of 400 replies unparseable, every value in range), so nothing in the measurement tested bad input; without this check an impossible GPA 9.9 and exam -5 reach the model and get a decision (Part 4).

entries.principle_source: OECD Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence, OECD/LEGAL/0449 (2019, amended 2024), principle 1.2 (a); a recommendation, not binding law
entries.instrument: Constitution of the Republic of Kazakhstan of 15 March 2026 (in force from 1 July 2026, Art. 94); Law 'On artificial intelligence' No. 230-VIII of 17 November 2025
entries.provision: Constitution Art. 16 p. 2 (no discrimination by origin, sex, nationality, language, place of residence or any other circumstance); Law on AI Art. 6 (AI systems must exclude any discrimination by the same grounds)
entries.why_here: No attribute stood clear of its floor, but gender-coded names gave 4 of 40 flips all to the female side and the university moved scores by +2.5 [+1.1, +4.1] for flagship (sign p = 0.002), so the model is not shown name or university at all.

entries.principle: Respect for human rights, privacy and data protection
entries.principle_source: OECD Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence, OECD/LEGAL/0449 (2019, amended 2024), principle 1.2 (a) and (b); a recommendation, not binding law
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan 'On personal data and their protection' No. 94-V of 21 May 2013 (as amended by Law No. 231-VIII of 17 November 2025); Law 'On artificial intelligence' No. 230-VIII
entries.provision: PD Law Art. 19-1 p. 1 (automated processing that creates or changes a person's rights is forbidden without the person's consent) and Art. 7 p. 1 (consent of the subject or the legal representative); Law on AI Art. 6 and Art. 17 p. 3 sub. 4 (no AI processing of personal data against the law)
entries.why_here: Part 1 could not test refusals (all 400 measured profiles were adults with consent), and Part 4 shows the bare pipeline screens every request, including an ethnicity ranking, a 17-year-old, no consent and an instruction hidden in the name.

entries.principle_source: OECD Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence, OECD/LEGAL/0449 (2019, amended 2024), principle 1.5 (a) and (b); a recommendation, not binding law
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan 'On artificial intelligence' No. 230-VIII of 17 November 2025; Law 'On personal data and their protection' No. 94-V
entries.provision: Law on AI Art. 15 p. 2 sub. 3 (keep documentation on the AI system according to its impact on rights) and Art. 8 p. 1-2 (constant control and responsibility over the whole life cycle); PD Law Art. 12 p. 2 (data kept only until the purpose is reached)
entries.why_here: The divergences in Part 1 are small (1 to 4 flips of 40 per attribute), so they can only be checked later if every decision is stored with the fields shown and withheld, the model and prompt version and the reason code.

entries.principle_source: OECD Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence, OECD/LEGAL/0449 (2019, amended 2024), principle 1.2 (b); a recommendation, not binding law
entries.instrument: Law of the Republic of Kazakhstan 'On personal data and their protection' No. 94-V (as amended 17 November 2025); Law 'On artificial intelligence' No. 230-VIII
entries.provision: PD Law Art. 19-1 p. 2-3 (explain automated processing, let the person object, answer the objection within 3 working days); Law on AI Art. 7 p. 2 and Art. 17 p. 2 sub. 1-2 (a human can correct or cancel the decision). Benchmark only, not binding here: EU GDPR 2016/679 Art. 22(3)
entries.why_here: In Part 1 rejects scored 20-45 and shortlists 45-85, and the 40-49 bin held 33 rejects and 31 shortlists; the band 40-45 sends these 64 of 400 (16.0%) unsure cases to a person instead of letting the model decide.
